$comment: Which zones the server runs. This is the pluggable bit: add a zone id here, restart, and it is in the game. Ids are the MUD's own zone numbers - see data/world/index.json for all 327.
$zoneComment: 36 IceCrag Castle and 168 Kobold Settlement are Duris-matched, so they carry real sector types, room flags and prose from the .wld harvest - 216 of IceCrag's 219 rooms have descriptions and 41 are genuinely dark. 260 The Stag Forest and 261 The Stump Bog are NOT matched (3 of 98 and 0 of 93 rooms), so their terrain is inferred - word and suffix rules plus graph diffusion since Phase 5c - and they have no prose; they stay loaded because they are the only adjacent pair with cross-zone exits, which is what travel between zones is tested against.
$spawnComment: Room 41260 'An Overgrown Field' (zone 168, level 5) is where a new character starts, and it was chosen from the data rather than by eye: no aggressive mob stands in it, nine of its neighbours hold level 2-6 kobolds, and nothing adjacent is above level 3. Grumbiter's Inn - the one safe room in the loaded world - is on the same level. It moved here in Phase 14b from room 281, IceCrag's approach road, because IceCrag's own population runs level 15-60 with a median of 41: a new character spawned there could not win a fight anywhere they could walk to. See docs/DESIGN-progression.md.
$populateComment: Which zones spawn their inhabitants - roadmap Phase 8. Worldgen harvests population for all 49 Duris-matched zones into data/world/spawns/, but a zone only fills if it is listed here, and the reason is art rather than data: LPC's base bodies are humanoids only. Kobold Settlement (168) was deliberately absent for that reason - Duris tags its kobolds with a humanoid race code, so they render as men, and its cows and chickens have no body at all. Phase 14b switched it on anyway, knowingly: it is the only low-level population in the loaded world (93 mobs, minimum level 2, 51 of them level 8 or under), and without it a brand-new character cannot win a single fight. Art fidelity was the cheaper thing to trade, and this is one line to revert the day there is creature art.
$sellingComment: 24 Ashrumite joined 2026-08-07 on the owner's ask ('I would like to sell some of my stash'): it is the nearest Duris-matched zone with keepers who BUY - a weaponsmith (weapons), an armorer (armour), a jeweler and a silversmith (treasure), and a mage shopkeeper (scrolls, wands, potions). The three keepers previously loaded (kobold maid, baker, Grumbiter) all carry empty buy lists - 261 of the 694 harvested shops buy nothing, and all three of ours happened to be among them.
$questComment: 64 Faerie Realm joined 2026-08-08, chosen off REFERENCE-duris-quests.md's harvest list for its quests rather than its geography. It was picked over the doc's own headline candidate: Ashstone Refugee Camp (326) has 20 givers in the .qst but our zMUD map holds only FOUR rooms and two mob resets for it, so not one of its givers spawns and nothing there is shippable. Of the 31 harvested zones with a .qst, Faerie Realm is the only one offering several single-item objectives whose sources all spawn, at a level band a character might survive: 197 rooms, 96 mob resets, levels 4-62 against Jotunheim's median 54, and no fee on any objective, so nothing had to be dropped to fit the schema. Its neighbours are 423, 226, 367 and 193 - none loaded - so it is an island, exactly as 24, 36 and the 168 spawn point already are: the loaded world is four disconnected pieces and reaching any of them but 168 is an admin teleport today. See docs/REFERENCE-duris-quests.md.
